same_canonical_owner_every_case.result: C1 and C2 used exact entry identifiers; C3 used the generic phrase Factorium reference method in all three cases.

majority_required_core_categories.result: All required categories are populated; C1 and C2 reproduce each complete canonical root factorization while C3 selects partial factor sets.

authority_and_projection_loss_preserved.result: All coders retain source authority boundaries and describe projection loss in every case.

graph_sufficiency_answered.result: All nine case records say a generic property graph is representationally sufficient.

majority_essential_domain_extension.result: Access has partial enforcement-lifecycle overlap; quantity has broad basis/state overlap; choice has no stable majority across outcome-cell, generation-boundary, and recommendation-authority proposals.

terminology_advantage.result: Preferences split one Formography, one governed-property-graph, and one neither.

unanimous_findings: A generic property graph is representationally sufficient in every case.
Source authority and projection loss must remain explicit.
The governed-method-profile thesis is not falsified solely by representation.
disagreements: Canonical form-owner identification is not unanimous.
The smallest essential domain extension is unstable.
The most consequential structured failure differs across coders.
No terminology option has a majority explanation-cost advantage.
next_test: Pre-register a V1 adjudication ontology for owner identity, core-category agreement, and extension equivalence without exposing authored answers, then run new coders. Retain the V0 records unchanged.
